292a2165ca76645d.description: About Maaden Maaden, established in 1997, is recognized as one of the fastest-growing mining companies globally and the largest multi-commodity mining and metals company in the Middle East. The company is instrumental in developing the mining industry to become a key pillar of Saudi Arabia’s economy by building an integrated mining value chain. Role Overview The Principal Specialist, Data Modeling & Arch (Operational Technology) will establish the data modeling and architecture foundation for Operational Technology (OT) and industrial data across plants, sites, and operational systems. This full-time role, based in Riyadh, is crucial for enabling trusted OT analytics by standardizing data representation, governance, and alignment with enterprise IT data products for assets, tags, events, alarms, measurements, production contexts, historians, SCADA/DCS, and condition monitoring data. Key Responsibilities Define enterprise OT data modeling standards for time-series data, events, alarms, assets, tags, measurements, and production contexts. Establish canonical OT concepts including asset hierarchy, location hierarchy, tag naming, measurement definitions, and work order linkage. Design scalable data schemas for curated OT layers and reusable OT data products with auditability, lineage, and quality attributes. Architect OT-to-IT data alignment patterns that connect operational measurements with enterprise entities for reporting and analytics. Define integration rules for tag mapping, unit standardization, reference data, semantic consistency, and cross-site normalization. Embed governance-by-design into OT data models, including ownership, metadata, lineage, quality rules, and lifecycle controls. Partner with OT engineering, cybersecurity, data platform, and infrastructure teams to design secure and compliant OT data flows. Review solution designs, data models, vendor deliverables, and integration approaches to ensure architectural consistency. Provide technical leadership on OT semantics, industrial data architecture, data modeling practices, and data product design. Lucid operates with deep vertical integration, handling design, engineering, and production in-house across its global offices and manufacturing facilities. Teams at Lucid are united by a commitment to excellence, aiming to redefine possibilities in mobility. The Role of Sr. Engineer, Closures Mechanisms/Plastics - Doors The Sr. Engineer, Closures Mechanisms/Plastics - Doors is responsible for ensuring the design intent assembly requirements of closure mechanisms and plastics on the manufacturing line. This full-time role serves as the technical lead for product issue root cause analysis and deviation containment, supporting product launches as the primary engineering contact for Mechanisms/Plastics. The position also involves sustaining engineering post-launch, including the design and release of new parts to enhance quality or assembly processes. The Sr. Engineer will collaborate with core engineering to ensure parts meet all design and validation requirements. Key Responsibilities Assume ownership of Closures Mechanisms and plastic system assembly. Solve complex component/system level problems using standard problem-solving techniques to determine root cause and provide containment solutions. Ensure design intent assembly requirements for closure systems are enforced on the assembly line. Implement data-driven proactive problem-solving and issue avoidance strategies for process deviations or critical part quality issues. Support new product launches and execute part concession deviations for Closures Mechanisms/Plastics components within the manufacturing plant. Collaborate with manufacturing teams to ensure efficient process sequencing and build quality. Manage sustaining engineering for automotive Closures Hardware and mechanism parts and assemblies, including Side Door Window regulators and glass, Handles, Latches, Checkers, Power actuators, Charge Port mechanisms, and plastic trim parts such as Side Door Exterior Rocker Trims, Side Door functional plastic parts (glass run channels, close out panels), Hood Trims, Liftgate trims, and Spoiler Systems. Work with various stakeholders and attribute owners across the company (*, Vehicle Safety, Vehicle Dynamics, NVH, Durability, Manufacturing, Design Studio) to validate design solutions. Engage cross-functionally with Manufacturing, Design, Product Development, Purchasing, Supplier Quality, Stamping, and Suppliers on tasks such as tool buy-offs and secondary component changes. Coordinate and communicate with interfacing suppliers. Provide direction to others and negotiate balanced solutions effectively. Coordinate virtual engineering and physical validation testing activities for designs. Travel domestically and internationally as required. Qualifications and Requirements Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical or Automotive Engineering disciplines with 5+ years of automotive experience in design and release of vehicle attributes, or a Master of Science degree in Mechanical or Automotive disciplines with 5+ years of automotive experience in design and release of vehicle attributes. Experience working with Class A surface data. Professional certification in Six Sigma (Black Belt or Green Belt), Shainin RedX, or an equivalent problem-solving methodology. Hands-on practical experience in prototype and production assembly, including a willingness to assemble parts directly. Proficiency with 3D CAD systems such as CATIA or similar software. Experience in technology, system, and supplier selection. Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment. Detail-oriented approach with a determined problem-solving attitude, utilizing an Engineering first principles approach. Design release engineering experience, including engineering change management and project management. Demonstrated excellence in previous positions, showcasing creativity in resolving mechanical design problems. Experience in full life cycle development from concept to prototype to full production. Knowledge of manufacturing processes applicable to Closures hardware and mechanisms, such as injection molding, die castings, stampings, ultrasonic welding, and bonding.

PURPOSE OF THE POSITION The Support Manager consolidates under a single leadership the technical know-how, information systems, supply chain, inventory and investment project functions of Metals, ensuring that the operating divisions receive consistent, timely and fact-based support. The position exists to guarantee that technical knowledge is captured, standardised and transferred across the organisation; that information systems and data integrity underpin management decisions; that materials, supplies and inventories are managed with the accuracy and discipline required by a non-ferrous manufacturing environment; and that investment projects are centrally structured, evaluated and followed through to completion. The role operates primarily on a project basis: each priority initiative is set up as a defined project with objectives, scope, resources, milestones and measurable results, coordinating the contribution of the different areas involved.
